dramatic.state_in: Greg wants another external thread test after mixed results.
dramatic.required_result: Hessa decides the apparatus is too noisy and redirects attention to internally repeatable control.
dramatic.state_out: Greg accepts the strongest evidence is his control sequence, then fails a changed directional cue usefully.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns attempt budget; Greg owns report.

performance.pressure: Greg reads stopping the thread test as abandoning possibility.
performance.behavior: Hessa reviews all three attempts, then tests whether Greg follows current direction or prepared target.
performance.relationship: Conflict is about safe use of scarce attempts.

screenplay: The thread apparatus is gone; Greg notices before sitting.
Hessa reviews all three external attempts and names the reliable part: Greg's internal sequence.
She marks a target and lets him establish a localized alteration.
Then she changes the directional cue away from the prepared mark.
Greg's edge sharpens toward the old target; he reports the wrong direction.
RETURN works cleanly. Direction question fails; general control does not.

audit.rhythm: SOURCE_WIN: evidence claims and cue-change need discrete boundaries

dramatic.required_result: Test direction-first shaping with no prepared destination using elbowward.
dramatic.state_out: Greg reports a small asymmetry on the instructed side, increasing confidence while remaining self-report.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns wording/evidence strength; Greg owns sensation and certainty.

performance.behavior: Hessa separates direction from her pointing hand; Greg reports uncertainty instead of forcing a clean answer.
performance.relationship: Shared discipline is becoming a skill.

screenplay: Blank forearm, no target. Hessa defines elbowward as direction, not destination.
Greg establishes a neutral localized alteration.
On directional cue he waits through uncertainty rather than forcing change.
The elbow-side boundary seems to sharpen while wrist side stays.
On RETURN the distinction softens first, then the rest fades.
Hessa records instructed-side asymmetry with no independent confirmation.

audit.rhythm: SOURCE_WIN: uncertainty and boundary observations are distinct states

dramatic.state_in: Two opposite direction-first reports suggest emerging directional control.
dramatic.state_out: A third internally consistent directional report lets Hessa call narrow directional control provisionally supported.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns threshold wording; Greg owns subjective report.

performance.pressure: Greg wants the category; Hessa makes him earn it.
performance.behavior: Greg distrusts a fast response but reports it; Hessa makes him report sensation rather than argument.
performance.relationship: Payoff works because Hessa has consistently refused premature milestones.

screenplay: Hessa announces replication, not novelty.
Greg shapes a neutral patch with no prepared target.
On wristward cue the wrist-side edge sharpens almost immediately; Greg distrusts speed.
Hessa tells him to report sensation, not argument.
RETURN reduces cleanly with no motor response.
Hessa upgrades the claim to provisionally supported under this narrow condition.

audit.rhythm: SOURCE_WIN: yes/no boundaries negotiate the claim

dramatic.state_in: Greg's mobility is good enough for small courier work but still requires adaptation.
dramatic.required_result: Make a bounded delivery demonstrate practical independence without pretending crutch travel is solved.
dramatic.state_out: Greg returns useful and more aware of environment/body interaction.
dramatic.ownership: Greg owns route/pacing; employer owns task/result.

performance.pressure: Ordinary work must stay ordinary enough to matter.
performance.behavior: Greg evaluates geometry, chooses around bad surfaces, and accepts slower movement without turning obstacles into lessons.
performance.relationship: Work treats him as capable within constraints.

screenplay: Greg takes a small route-based job because someone needs it done.
He tests bag position against crutch swing before leaving.
On the street he chooses broad road over mud despite extra distance.
He handles stairs and a disputed receipt without heroics.
He returns signed/annotated slips rather than solving merchant problems.
The task closes as work, not therapy.

dramatic.state_in: Greg can localize an unfamiliar right-side alteration.
dramatic.required_result: Test a new intact-side target without falling into broader familiar patterns.
dramatic.state_out: A localized response appears closer to instruction without establishing general control.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns test question; Greg owns report.

performance.pressure: Greg wants each good-looking result to become a milestone.
performance.behavior: Hessa prevents scoring and keeps the target coarse; Greg stops excitement before it changes the attempt.
performance.relationship: Mutual competence is visible through disagreement.

screenplay: Hessa draws a charcoal dot near the little-finger knuckle.
She defines the question as one unfamiliar localized alteration, not perfect finger magic.
Greg draws and attempts one small change toward the mark.
A patch forms near target without wrist rotation or broad hand spread.
He releases and reports before hearing her observation.
Hessa confirms localized change and immediately limits the claim.
